title: SDK First 90 Days: Playbook and Lab Recipes
author: Riya Patel
summary: A structured 90-day onboarding and ramp plan for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs. Includes weekly milestones, micro-labs, canonical support fixes, telemetry checks, and rollback recipes tailored for production inference clients.
content:
Purpose
This document defines a repeatable "first 90 days" experience for engineers (new hires or internal integrators) who are building production integrations using Redwood SDKs. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success, improve telemetry coverage, and codify canonical fixes for the top support issues we see in the first three months.

Scope
- Applies to all SDKs: JavaScript, Python, Go, and internal runtime adapters.
- Focused on engineering ramp (not hiring or HR onboarding).
- Cross-team checkpoints with DevX, Runtime, and SRE.

Quick start at a glance (90-day experience map)
- Week 0 (Prep): Create account, obtain dev token, clone sample repo, run smoke test.
- Weeks 1–2 (First calls): Complete 3 micro-labs (hello-gen, streaming, embeddings), add basic telemetry.
- Weeks 3–6 (Product integration): Wire SDK into feature flow, add prefix caching, pick batching strategy.
- Weeks 7–10 (Scale & quality): Load-test client patterns, enable canary routing, validate model fallback.
- Weeks 11–12 (Stabilize): Finalize SLOs, long-tail error monitoring, schedule QBR with Runtime.

Micro-labs (hands-on recipes)
Each lab is designed to be 30–90 minutes and runnable locally. Labs include goals, commands, expected outputs, and quick diagnostics.

1) Lab: Hello-generation (JS + Python)
- Objective: Make a simple generation call and render streamed tokens.
- Steps:
  1. Install the SDK: npm i @redwood/inference (or pip install redwood-inference).
  2. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and run sample: node examples/hello-gen.js or python examples/hello_gen.py.
  3. Verify output: streamed token lines, final JSON with tokens_count.
- Sanity checks:
  - 401: validate API key and environment variable name.
  - 429: ensure local test isn’t running heavy parallel calls; add rate-limit guard.
- Expected telemetry:
  - span.client_call (latency_ms), metric.tokens_generated, log.sample_id.

2) Lab: Streaming resume and idempotency (JS)
- Objective: Demonstrate resume tokens + idempotent replay for flaky networks.
- Commands (shell):
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  - node examples/stream-resume-demo.js --simulate-drop
- Observability goals:
  - Every stream must emit partial_chunk and final_chunk events.
  - If a resume occurs, trace must include resume_attempt:true.

3) Lab: Embeddings joiner (Python)
- Objective: Compute batched embeddings and compare recall under two batching configs.
- Sample config (JSON):
  {
    "batch_max_tokens": "1024",
    "batch_max_items": "64",
    "batch_timeout_ms": "20"
  }
- Verification: cosine similarity scores should match expected fixture (>= 0.85 for same-doc pairs).

Canonical fixes for top early-support issues
We collect fixes engineers should attempt before escalating to support. Apply these in order:
- Issue: Intermittent 403 when running on CI
  - Fixes: 1) Confirm token has project scope; 2) Check CI runner time drift (sync NTP); 3) Ensure no token rotation during run.
- Issue: High tail latency for short requests
  - Fixes: 1) Disable large-batch pooling; 2) Use small-sequence optimized model variant (v2-small); 3) Add prefix KV caching for repeated contexts.
- Issue: Streaming truncates mid-response
  - Fixes: 1) Inspect network MTU and proxy buffering; 2) Verify client auto-reconnect/resume logic; 3) Compare trace ids to server logs and open runtime ticket with trace id.

Telemetry & dashboard checklist (required signals)
Add these metrics/traces to the integration before Week 4:
- Metrics (per-route): rps, p50/p90/p99 latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_rate
- Traces: request_id, model_variant, route, batch_size, resume_attempt, fallback_used
- Logs: client_version, user_agent, sample_id, prompt_hash

Suggested Grafana dashboard panels (text table)
| Panel | Query | Alert threshold | Owner |
|------|-------|----------------|-------|
| SDK Errors | sum(rate(sdk_request_errors[5m])) | > 0.5% | Runtime SRE |
| Tail Latency | percentile(latency_ms, 99) by route | > 1200ms | Runtime |
| Token Cost | sum(tokens_out) / sum(requests) | > baseline+15% | Product Ops |

Canary rollout and rollback recipe (for SDK-driven feature flags)
1) Create canary config with 5% traffic and model fallback to cheaper variant.
2) Deploy client with telemetry gate enabled.
3) Monitor p99 latency and error_rate over 30 minutes.
4) Escalate conditions (auto-rollback):
   - p99 > 2x baseline for 30m OR error_rate > 1% for 10m.
5) Rollback steps (CLI snippets):
   - redwood canary set --id <id> --traffic 0
   - redwood deploy promote --previous
   - Open incident channel (#sdk-oncall) and attach traces.

SLOs & acceptance criteria for go-to-production
- Functional: 100% of non-flaky unit tests pass + deterministic golden prompt outputs for smoke suite.
- Reliability: p95 < 400ms, p99 < 1200ms for generation APIs under canary load.
- Observability: 95% of requests carry trace headers and contain sample_id.
- Cost: tokens_per_request within 15% of baseline estimate for the integration class.

Support escalation matrix (who to call)
- Tier 1: DevX triage (channel: #devx-support) — fast reproductions and SDK patches.
- Tier 2: Runtime SRE (oncall) — traces, kernel-level issues, sudden capacity regressions.
- Tier 3: Model & Research — quality regressions or hallucination patterns.
- Required artifacts before escalation:
  1) Repro script or minimal repo.
  2) Trace ids, timestamps, region, model_variant.
  3) SDK version and environment (node/python versions).

Diagnostics runbook (fast checklist)
1) Reproduce locally with sample repo and --capture-trace flag.
2) Check SDK telemetry: confirm span.client_call exists and contains server_trace_id.
3) Inspect server-side logs for trace id and TTL mismatches.
4) If network: run tcpdump for 60s on client and server side and attach to ticket.

Ownership and support SLAs
- Primary owner: DevX SDK team (devx-leads@redwood.ai).
- Runtime SRE provides 24x7 oncall for infra incidents.
- Escalation SLA: DevX responds to new triage tickets within 2 business hours, SRE within 30 minutes for P1.

Appendix A — sample CLI and config snippets
- Example: quick local smoke (bash)
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
  git clone git@github.com:redwood/integration-samples.git
  cd integration-samples/hello-gen
  # install & run
  npm ci && node examples/hello-gen.js

- Example: SDK client config (YAML)
  sdk:
    telemetry_enabled: true
    batch: { max_items: 32, timeout_ms: 25 }
    resume_retries: 2

Appendix B — learning resources and workshops
- Weekly office hours: DevX Labs (Wednesdays 10:00 PT).
- Recommended reading: "SDK Observability Cookbook" (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-observability-telemetry-cookbook-2026).
- Graduation checklist: demo integration to Runtime team, pass smoke suite on Dedicated environment, and sign-off on cost projection.

FAQ (short)
- Q: When do I switch from dev token to project-scoped token?
  - A: Before systems integration tests (Week 3).
- Q: Who owns the golden prompt suite?
  - A: Product + DevX; maintain in repo: infra/goldens/prompts.json.
